chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Long-Haired Bob and his four kinds of blues
summary: His stepfather points out the trumpeter Long-Haired Bob, who played only blues for the lowest strata, including the Slow Slow Slow Drag.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: My stepfather told me one day... I saw this guy when I was with my uncle. He said, "That's a trumpet player." I said, "How do you know?" He said, "Well, you see his lip? He's got a red lip spot on his lip." So I said, "You don't have to be a trumpet player..." No, a cornet player. "He don't have to be a cornet player because he's got a red spot on his lip." So I criticized(?) my stepfather. He said, "It might not, but he's a trumpet player." I said, "Who is he?" He said, "That's Long-Haired Bob."

So I've got to put Long-Haired Bob in there. I had never seen Long-Haired Bob play. But they told me about him. Long-Haired Bob had this funky Blues band. He played nothin' but Blues. A real professor of Blues. He played four styles of Blues. Blues, Slow Blues, Fast Blues, and the Slow-Slow-Slow Drag. When you hired Long-Haired Bob, all he did was play the Blues. And that Slow-Slow-Slow Drag was the fightin' Blues, because you'd do a whole lot of wigglin' and shakin'. And he played for people that was on the real lower level of the strata, who didn't give a damn. They drank... They worked hard, they lived hard, and they drank, and they wouldn't have nobody's music... They wouldn't hire no Louis Armstrong, King Oliver, nobody else they'd hire but Long-Haired Bob. Because Long-Haired Bob played Slow Blues, Fast Blues, Medium Blues, and the Slow-Slow-Slow Drag.
